chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah and Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari both narrated to us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fuddal, on the authority of Abu Jamilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The servants have not been commanded except according to their capacity. Therefore, whatever thing Allah commanded people to do, they are capable of doing it; and whatever they are not capable of doing, it has been placed (lifted) from them. However, there is no good in people (who do not fulfill their obligations).

key_terms.لا خير فيهم: There is no good in them (a phrase indicating lack of merit or virtue)
key_terms.موضوع: Placed, lifted, or removed (as in lifting the burden of obligation)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between divine commands and human capability in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the Shia principle of *al-Taklif bi-ma yutaq* (burden according to capacity), affirming that divine commands are never excessive relative to human ability. The concluding remark, 'but people have no good in them,' serves as a subtle critique of human negligence, suggesting that while capacity is granted, the actual merit depends on the conscious effort to utilize that capacity. This reinforces the theological balance between divine grace in assigning duties and human responsibility in executing them.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 6. My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) both said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah and `Abd Allah ibn Ja`far al-Himyari both said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn `Ali ibn Fuddal, on the authority of Abu Jamilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Ali al-Halabi that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

The servants (of Allah) have not been commanded to do anything more than what they are capable of doing. Therefore, people re able to refrain from whatever they have been enjoined to refrain, and whatever they do not have the ability to refrain from has not been required of them. However, there is no good in people (who do not fulfill their religious obligations.)
